as_told.title: Mario runs out of Close Encounters screening
as_told.place_text: Theater on Main Street, Rapid City, South Dakota

tellings.quote: Later in the year, when Close Encounters [of the Third Kind] came out, the mailbox scene freaked me out so badly that I had to get up and walk out of the theatre.

plain: In 1977 a former Air Force missile guard named Mario Woods, who says he had been abducted at a nuclear missile site, went to see the film Close Encounters of the Third Kind in Rapid City, South Dakota, and had to flee the theatre. He tells Michels he got up and ran out and sat on the curb on Main Street, because what he saw on screen "felt as if it was a direct replay of what I just went through". In a later episode, where he reunites with other veterans, he tells it more briefly: "I got up and took off." The researcher and writer Robert Hastings had already recorded the same memory in an article published on September 10, 2017, about Woods's apparent abduction at a missile site. There Woods is quoted as saying that "the mailbox scene freaked me out so badly that I had to get up and walk out of the theatre." Told this way across years, the story is offered as a sign that the film touched something Woods had really lived through.
